title: Deployment Commander Shift Roster & Snapshot Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick operational playbook for the on-call Deployment Commander(s) during medium-to-large cutovers. Focused on human handoffs, snapshot capture points, and minimal-burst rollback triggers.

Context / when to use this doc:
- Use for any multi-region deployment that requires staggered traffic migration and at least two live-phase handoffs (canary -> regional ramp -> global).
- Intended to be a lightweight runbook to run alongside the full release checklist; captures ephemeral decisions and snapshot artifacts that are often missing from postmortems.

Commander shift roster (recommended coverage model):
- Pre-cutover commander (T-+6h to T-+2h): Owner: Priya D.
  - Responsibilities: validate preflight snapshots, confirm capacity reservations, run synthetic smoke suite (basic API + auth), escalate blockers.
- Cutover commander (T-+2h to T+3h): Owner: Ava M. (primary), Noah C. (secondary)
  - Responsibilities: lead the cutover channel, execute traffic switch steps, call rollback if SLO breach or major error trend.
- Post-cutover commander (T+3h to T+12h): Owner: Liam O.
  - Responsibilities: keep watch on regression alerts, coordinate hotfixes, confirm stability for handoff to normal oncall.

Shift handoff checklist (to be read out on Slack huddle):
- Current step and expected state (e.g., "canary 30% in us-west, baseline latency < 110ms").
- Live telemetry snapshot links (APM dashboard, token-level cost graph, error budget burn rate).
- Active mitigations / retries in place.
- Pending PRs that touch routing, model pin, or autoscaler configs (list PR numbers).
- Who to call for infra escalation (pager ids).

Snapshot points (what to capture and where):
- Preflight: infra-state.json (autoscaler settings, pool sizes), model-artifact-id, config hash.
- Canary start: canary-snapshot_<timestamp>.log (sampling of request IDs and responses), canary-telemetry.csv (latency pctls, error counts).
- Canary 50%: compare token-cost-per-req and tail-latency to preflight.
- Post-cutover 1h/3h/12h: integrated snapshot with request traces for any error spikes.

Operational smoke/telemetry checks (order of priority):
1) API basic health (200s on health endpoint across AZs).
2) Latency SLA check (p50/p95/p99 thresholds).
3) Error rate delta vs baseline (5-min window).
4) Model output sanity tests (5 deterministic prompts against pinned model hash).
5) Cost telemetry sanity (unexpected token spike).

Automated rollback triggers (suggested, commander discretion override allowed):
- >3x baseline 5-min error rate sustained for 10 minutes.
- P95 increase > 2x baseline causing downstream queuing/backpressure.
- Model hallucination regression failing critical evals (linked eval set).

Communication templates (copy-paste into #release-ops during steps):
- Canary start: "[Canary START] canary 10% -> 30% in us-west. Commander: @AvaM. Preflight snapshots captured: <link>. Monitor p95 <= 120ms."
- Canary health OK: "[Canary HEALTHY] 30m check passed. p95 stable. Proceeding to regional ramp."
- Rollback call: "[ROLLBACK] Commander invoking rollback to previous stable config (artifact id: X). Rolling traffic back to stable pools. See rollback runbook: <link>."

Staggered calendar (key windows) - sample for a 1-day op: 2026-07-06
- 06:00–08:00 UTC: Preflight & infra reservations (quiet window).
- 08:00–09:30 UTC: Canary 10% -> 30% in us-west; 30m checks at +30m and +60m.
- 09:30–11:00 UTC: Regional ramps (us-west -> us-east -> eu-west) with 20–40m stabilization between regions.
- 11:00–14:00 UTC: Global traffic steering to new variant; extended monitoring and mitigation window.
- 14:00–18:00 UTC: Post-cutover stability watch, handoff to oncall rotation.

Release notes draft (short-form to paste into changelog):
- Infra: increased autoscaler burst capacity and introduced memory-limiter for batch workers.
- Serving runtime: upgraded kernel selection heuristics to prefer grouped attention for medium seq (QKV-optimizations).
- API: added a /healthz/token-cost endpoint for per-token accounting and early cost alerts.
- Rollouts: new staged traffic policy (region-first) and deployment-commander shift roster guidance.

Open questions / things to resolve before final publish:
- Decide default canary duration (30 vs 60 minutes) for latency-sensitive customers.
- Finalize who is the backup pager for international weekend cutovers.
- Confirm log retention for canary snapshots (currently 7 days; legal wants 90 days for some customers).

Quick links (for commander):
- Canary tracking dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/kanary
- Rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood/display/ENG/Rollback+Runbook
- Pager roster: https://handbook.redwood/pager-roster
- Evaluation set (canary sanity prompts): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/canary-sets

After-action note template (to paste in the release retrospective doc):
- Commander(s): [names]
- Cutover start/end times: [Tstart - Tend]
- Major issues: [short bullets]
- Snapshots collected: [links]
note: This doc is intentionally conversational; it's an operational aide for commanders to capture ephemeral state, not the canonical long-form release checklist. Move any finalized procedure to the main release checklist once agreed.
